method: Medians of complete cold-cache first deployments and real buu on separate macOS CI runners. Total time saved = 100 * (1 - candidate_seconds / Homebrew_seconds).
limitations: Two repetitions per workflow; real network and upstream metadata are variable.
Clean tests remove all runner formulae/casks before timing; Homebrew itself and OS/Xcode are preinstalled.
Query-only PR still uses Homebrew for initial install and every buu update/upgrade; observed timing variation is not a native fastbrew speedup.
conclusion: No attributable positive total-workflow speedup established. Current query-only MR does not accelerate initial installation or buu; causal savings for those workflows are zero. Native experiment has only one complete sample plus an unrelated upstream HTTP 500 failure, so observed percentages are not reliable backend performance estimates.

timed_workload.first_install: Empty default /opt/homebrew Cellar/Caskroom and empty API/bottle cache; full 66-declaration Brewfile plus dependencies, trusted taps/casks, dotfiles and Fisher bootstrap. Homebrew and OS already exist.
timed_workload.buu: Actual literal alias, including Homebrew self/API/tap update, inventory/dependency checks, downloads, checksums, install/upgrade/cleanup, and real Fisher update. Identical old bear 4.2.2, fastfetch 2.69.0, vchewing 4.8.8; all other Brewfile packages present/current; new bottle/pkg cache empty.
timed_workload.native_experiment: Native core formula bootstrap plus Homebrew Bundle for remaining declarations; real Homebrew update and a benchmark-only translation of -y to native noninteractive unrestricted upgrade. No delegation in the successful matched buu.

native_successful_buu_breakdown.note: Download span from timestamped CI output; not isolated CPU time. This is one sample, not a steady-state network estimate.

same_image_previous_observations: The earlier query-only control also appeared 30–36% faster while executing the same Homebrew commands; that variation cannot be attributed to fastbrew.
